image.alt: Emperor penguins standing close together on the ice in a snowy wind.

sentences.text: Emperor penguins live in Antarctica, the coldest place on Earth.
In winter, the wind is icy and the air can be colder than minus forty degrees.
To stay warm, thousands of penguins stand close together in a big group called a huddle.
Each penguin is warmed by the bodies around it, and the group loses much less heat than one bird alone.
The penguins on the outside get the coldest wind.
So the huddle slowly shuffles, and birds take turns moving into the warm middle.
This way, every penguin gets a chance to warm up.

vocabulary.meaning: a group standing very close together
the icy land around the South Pole
to move slowly with small steps, feet close to the ground

questions.prompt: Why do emperor penguins huddle together?
questions.hint: The bodies around each penguin keep it warm, so the group stands close together.

questions.prompt: Why do the penguins take turns in the middle?

choices.text: The food is in the middle
The outside of the huddle is the coldest place

questions.hint: The penguins on the outside get the coldest wind, so they take turns in the warm middle.

questions.prompt: What is this reading mostly about?

choices.text: How penguins share warmth in the cold

questions.hint: Almost every sentence tells how penguins keep warm together in the icy winter.

writing.prompt: Copy this sentence on the lines.
writing.model: Penguins huddle together to keep warm.

image.alt: A child standing on grass in the sunshine, with a long shadow stretching away from the Sun.

sentences.text: A shadow forms when something blocks light.
Light travels in straight lines, so it cannot bend around you to fill the space behind you.
That dark space on the ground is your shadow.
In the morning, the Sun is low in the sky, and your shadow is long.
At midday, the Sun is high above you, so your shadow is short.
In the evening, the Sun is low again, and your shadow stretches out the other way.
Your shadow always points away from the Sun.

vocabulary.meaning: a dark shape made when something blocks light
to stop something from getting through
the middle of the day, around twelve o'clock

questions.hint: A shadow forms when something blocks light, so the space behind it stays dark.
When the Sun is high above you, your shadow is short. The Sun is highest at midday.

writing.prompt: Finish the sentence on the lines.
writing.frame: My shadow is short at midday because ___.
